source: Plank & Wotawa (2026) Using SLMs and LLMs for Diagnosis, DX 2026
finding: 13 language models diagnosed faults in 7 small systems (3 electric circuits, heater, powertrain, hardware circuit, heater system). Scored by hand on correctness, completeness, reasoning, hallucination, uncertainty, clarity (0-2). Bigger models won clearly.
numbers: Hit rate / hallucination rate: Gemini 2.5 Flash 79.5% / 20.5%; Mistral Large 76.9% / 15.4%; Llama 4 Scout 17B 38.5% / 7.7%; most small models above 70% hallucination; Llama 3.2 1B 94.9%. Weighted score W: 1.846 (Gemini) down to 0.314 (TinyLlama).
quote: Well-known large language models performed best but still exhibit hallucinations and limitations in terms of correctness and completeness.
limits: Manual scoring, small example systems, only free models, 3 runs per case. Not a diagnosability test as such.
agent_relevance: Even the best models miss complete candidate sets, so a scaffold should not trust one free-text diagnosis; ask for the full candidate list and check it by code.

source: Plank & Wotawa (2026) Using SLMs and LLMs for Diagnosis, DX 2026 (completeness failure)
finding: In Circuit 1 Scenario 2, only Gemini 2.5 Flash named the valid but unlikely double fault (L1 and L2 both faulty). All other models listed only the most probable single faults. This is a direct case of models collapsing to one favoured diagnosis when the data allow several.
numbers: 1 of 13 models found the double-fault candidate in that scenario (as stated in text).
limits: One scenario; text states it, no repeated trials reported.
agent_relevance: Models prune low-prior multi-fault candidates early. Our agent should enumerate minimal candidates by rule (hitting sets) before ranking by likelihood.

source: Plank & Wotawa (2026) Phi-2 case study
finding: Phi-2 scored above 1.0 only on the powertrain (W = 1.05) while scoring 0.08 to 0.67 elsewhere. Outputs looked like textbook pages (candidate list then 'Follow-up Exercises'), so the authors call it training-data overlap, not reasoning.
numbers: Phi-2 W per system: 0.08, 0.30, 0.23, 0.35, 1.05 (powertrain), 0.34, 0.67. Three runs, all with unrequested exercise text.
limits: Interpretation is by the authors from output layout; not tested by a contamination probe.
agent_relevance: Benchmark success on textbook circuits can be memory. Test design should use unseen, hand-made systems.

source: Plank & Wotawa (2026) per-circuit scaling
finding: Complexity moderator: on Circuit 3 (most complex electric circuit) all small models fell below 0.60 and several near zero, while the three larger models stayed above 1.70. Size alone did not explain it: Mistral 7B (largest local model) fell behind Gemma-2 2B and Llama 3.2 3B there.
numbers: Circuit 3 W: Mistral 7B 0.33, Gemma-2 2B 0.55, Qwen2.5 3B 0.06, StableLM-2 0.10. Rank-sum ordering identical to W ordering for all 13 models.
limits: Single-author-team manual scoring; 7 systems only.
agent_relevance: Diagnostic reliability drops fast with system size; give the agent a code tool for consistency checks rather than relying on prose reasoning.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs?, DX 2025
finding: OpenAI models generated incidence matrices, minimal structurally overdetermined (MSO) sets, minimal conflicts and minimal diagnoses on hand-made arithmetic and logic circuits. These are the building blocks of diagnosis tests and of fault isolability analysis.
numbers: o3-mini: conflicts F1 = 0.917 +/- 0.249; diagnoses F1 = 0.784 +/- 0.322. o1 and o3-mini near perfect on incidence matrix; 4o-mini added extra variables. Performance fell as diagnoses count grew (up to about 150) and as relations grew (up to 14).
quote: LLMs do not provide an alternative to diagnosis algorithms. The current level of accuracy is not sufficient to replace traditional tools.
limits: Authors note run-to-run variance is high, cost and latency are unbounded, examples are small. gpt-4o and 4o-mini without code gave near-zero accuracy on unseen examples (footnote).
agent_relevance: Strong support for letting code (hitting sets, fault signature tables) compute diagnoses and distinguishing tests; the LLM should only formalise the model.

source: Marozzo & Lio (2026) LLM-as-an-Investigator, arXiv 2606.13220
finding: On 100 cases from 303 technical forum threads, an agent that keeps competing hypotheses and asks discriminating follow-up questions beat baselines. Having the right cause in the pool did not guarantee choosing it.
numbers: Final score /100 (95% CI): SIA 79.2 [72.7,83.7]; THK-int 72.8; Ask-5 72.3; ReAct 69.0; ToT 61.5; direct BAS 67.3; THK 67.5. Potential (oracle over pool): SIA 89.2, ToT 84.0. SIA asks 5.2 questions and records 9.0 hypotheses; ToT records 21.0 hypotheses.
quote: Broader exploration therefore does not necessarily produce better diagnostic selection.
limits: User simulator, forum-derived cases, one main backbone (Gemini); logging asymmetry between methods; potential is not always reachable if the discriminating observation is missing.
agent_relevance: Test design (S7) matters: more hypotheses without discriminating questions gives a pool-to-choice gap of 10 to 22 points. Matches diagnosability idea: if no observation separates two candidates, picking is guessing.

source: Marozzo & Lio (2026) ablation of SIA
finding: Ablations show which parts carry the gain. Removing structured investigation or counterfactual critique hurts most; removing hypothesis expansion hurts the pool; removing final adjudication hurts selection only.
numbers: Final/potential: full 79.2/89.2; no structured investigation 72.8/84.7; no counterfactual critique 74.0/85.5; no follow-up questions 75.0/85.0; no hypothesis expansion 76.5/79.3; no weight updates 78.5/88.5; no adjudication 76.0/89.2.
limits: Same 100 cases, one run setting, no significance test across ablations.
agent_relevance: Counterfactual 'what observation would separate these two' step is worth about 5 points; keep it as a distinct operator rather than folding it into a generic critique.

source: Marozzo & Lio (2026) cross-backbone and stress test
finding: Advantage held on two other backbones. A misleading but plausible user suggestion lowered scores and was selected as the answer in 2 of 10 paired cases.
numbers: GPT-5.6 Terra: SIA 75.4 final vs THK-int 69.2. Claude Sonnet 5: SIA 76.1 vs 68.4. Stress test, 10 pairs: final 80.0 control vs 76.0 challenged; exact diagnosis 6/10 vs 5/10; wrong suggested cause selected 2/10; lower than control 3/10.
limits: Only 10 pairs in stress test; wide uncertainty.
agent_relevance: Planted wrong hypotheses are a cheap robustness probe for our diagnosis operators.

source: Luo et al. (2026) Graph of States: abductive tasks with LLMs, arXiv 2603.21250
finding: A state machine plus causal graph of hypotheses and evidence beat CoT, ToT, GoT, FoT (single and multi-agent) on distributed-system failure diagnosis, at lower cost than the strongest baseline.
numbers: Distributed systems, LLM judge: GoS Match 70.67%, Relevant 88.00%, $0.10/case; best baseline Match 34.00% (Multi/CoT); Multi/FoT cost $0.94/case. Error rates GoS vs pooled baselines: evidence fabrication 0% vs 22.22%; context drift 9.70% vs 41.32%; early stopping 18.75% vs 63.89%; failed backtracking 30.90% vs 52.78%.
limits: Medical table in the extracted PDF text is misaligned, so GoS medical numbers are not recorded here. Wrong action selection stayed high (55.90% of GoS failures), attributed to domain knowledge.
agent_relevance: Strong precedent for our state-based scaffold: explicit hypothesis/evidence state removes fabricated evidence and early stopping. Early stopping at a coarse diagnosis is the same ambiguity problem diagnosability studies.

source: Luo et al. (2026) GoS ablation (medical diagnosis)
finding: Dropping the state machine or causal graph cut the Match rate sharply; plain structured text state gave only part of the gain, so the effect is not just context management.
numbers: Match (LLM judge): w/o reasoning focus 31.88; structured state without causal graph 19.57; w/o causal graph 18.12; w/o state machine 12.32. Cost rose to $0.17/case without state machine because it used the whole budget before stopping.
limits: Medical task, one benchmark, table partly garbled in extraction.
agent_relevance: Support for explicit stop rules: a state machine saves cost by forcing termination once evidence supports a candidate.

source: Miao, Jancar, Komenda, Masopust, Lai (2026) Diagnosability Verification for Automata and Petri Nets: Can We Do Better?
finding: Strong diagnosability of a monolithic automaton is checkable in quadratic time; conditional on the orthogonal vectors conjecture (SETH), no faster algorithm exists. Modular systems cannot beat quadratic on the composed monolith. Weak diagnosability has a new exponential algorithm shown optimal under ETH-type assumptions, and is undecidable for unbounded Petri nets.
numbers: Strong: quadratic in states. Weak (Cao et al. 2021): exponential in a power of the state count (exact exponent garbled in extracted text). Modular strong diagnosability not polynomial unless P = PSPACE (Yin & Lafortune 2017; Masopust & Yin 2019).
quote: verifying diagnosability of a modular system cannot be verified in polynomial-time unless P = PSPACE
limits: Complexity under conjectures, not empirical. Applies to discrete event models, not LLM text.
agent_relevance: Checking 'can any test ever separate these candidates' is cheap for small flat models and hard for modular ones, so cap model size and check flat.

source: Zhang & Raisch (2024) Diagnosability of labeled Dp-automata, arXiv 2109.07125
finding: Review of complexity results for diagnosability, and a retraction-style note: an earlier claimed polynomial algorithm actually runs in exponential time. For weighted automata over some dioids diagnosability verification is coNP-complete.
numbers: Twin plant gives polynomial test for plain automata. Decentralised diagnosability PSPACE-hard. Timed automata: PSPACE-complete (PSPACE-hard even for 2-clock). Another related problem 2-EXPTIME-complete.
quote: the algorithm runs in exponential time
limits: Theory; the flagged error is in an earlier paper cited as [20, Remark 2].
agent_relevance: A published polynomial claim for diagnosability was wrong. Treat complexity claims in sources with caution and verify by running code.

source: Rintanen & Grastien (2007) Diagnosability Testing with Satisfiability Algorithms, IJCAI
finding: Succinctly represented systems make diagnosability PSPACE-complete, but a SAT encoding of the twin plant finds non-diagnosability witnesses in systems with astronomic state counts where explicit twin plants cannot be built.
numbers: Components with 6 states each, 22 events (4 observable); explicit twin plant of 6^(2C) states infeasible from about C = 8. SAT handled 160 to 200 components. Formulas about 1-2 hundred thousand variables, 1-2 million clauses; runtimes grew exponentially (examples 5.55 s to 20.48 s on a 1.73 GHz Pentium 4 for satisfiable cases); unsatisfiable (n=3) cases about 0.01-0.06 s.
limits: Synthetic regular chain of identical components; authors say harder component structure or longer cycles may not scale.
agent_relevance: Non-diagnosability is a bounded-length search for two observation-identical runs, one with the fault and one without. Our agent can phrase this as 'find two candidates giving the same readings'.

source: Ibrahim, Dague, Grastien, Ye, Simon (2017) Diagnosability Planning for Controllable DES, AAAI-17
finding: If a system is not diagnosable, find one action sequence that moves it to a diagnosable belief state, then let it run. Diagnosability planning is PSPACE-complete, easier than active diagnosability (EXPTIME-complete). Reusing twin-plant parts sped search.
numbers: Eager Learning about 15 times faster than the plain method on a grid of height 50 (width 3); eager method scaled to initial belief of 500 states (10x10 grid) where the plain method exploded around 45 states.
limits: Synthetic grid benchmark built by the authors; sensitivity to design of benchmark.
agent_relevance: Design the test first, then wait: make a short plan of probes that makes candidates separable, instead of probing at random.

source: Su, Zanella, Grastien (2016) Diagnosability of DES with Uncertain Observations, IJCAI
finding: Diagnosability can still hold when observations are uncertain in order or value. The twin plant is extended with compound observable events; a fault is diagnosable iff the verifier twin has no loop of ambiguous states (Theorem 1). Verifier size is O(|X|^2 |Sigma_o|).
numbers: Verifier size O(|X|^2 |Sigma_o|) per fault; no empirical benchmark figures extracted.
limits: Theory-focused; I did not extract experiment tables.
agent_relevance: Noisy tool outputs need not break diagnosis if the test set is diagnosable even under that noise; check separability against the noisy reading.

source: Zhang et al. (2019) Estimation and Verification of Partially-Observed DES (survey), arXiv 1903.11413
finding: Survey: detectability, diagnosability, prognosability, distinguishability and opacity can all be tested with observers or twin plants. Twin plant size is quadratic in system size, so diagnosability and distinguishability checks are polynomial for monolithic systems.
numbers: Algorithm complexity in survey: about O(|Sigma|^2 |X|^2) for the augmented-system method (line 361 of the text).
limits: Review of theory; no human or LLM data.
agent_relevance: Diagnosability is one member of a family: distinguishability asks whether two named candidates can be told apart, which is the question S7 needs for a pair.

source: Rintanen (2007) Diagnosers and diagnosability of succinct transition systems (cited in b13 and b14)
finding: Cited by two opened papers as the proof that diagnosability of succinctly represented systems is PSPACE-complete.
numbers: PSPACE-complete (as stated in b13 text).
limits: Cited only; I did not open the original.
agent_relevance: Same as b13.

source: Sampath, Sengupta, Lafortune, Sinnamohideen, Teneketzis (1995) Diagnosability of discrete-event systems, IEEE TAC 40(9)
finding: Founding definition and diagnoser-based test. Described in opened papers as exponential space in the number of states.
numbers: Exponential in system states (per b11, b13, b14).
limits: Cited via later papers; original not opened.
agent_relevance: Origin of the question 'does every fault give a distinguishable record after finite events'.

source: Jiang, Huang, Chandra, Kumar (2001) A polynomial algorithm for testing diagnosability of DES, IEEE TAC 46(8)
finding: Twin plant: pair two copies of the system and look for an infinite path of ambiguous pairs. Cited as polynomial. Later quadratic algorithm by Yoo & Lafortune (2002) and Moreira et al. (2011) per b11.
numbers: Twin plant size quadratic in states (b16). Impractical beyond about 10000 states (stated in b13).
limits: Cited via later papers; original not opened. Rintanen & Grastien state explicit pair enumeration is impractical at that size.
agent_relevance: The 'two runs, same readings, different fault status' pattern is directly usable as an agent check.

source: Yin & Lafortune (2017) and Masopust & Yin (2019) modular diagnosability hardness (cited in b11)
finding: Per b11: modular diagnosability cannot be verified in polynomial time unless P = PSPACE, even when all shared events are observable.
numbers: PSPACE-hardness conditional on P != PSPACE.
limits: Reported via b11, originals not read.
agent_relevance: Large decomposed systems may need heuristics, not exact tests.

source: Cao et al. (2021) weak diagnosability algorithm (cited in b11)
finding: Per b11: weak diagnosability (a way to detect the fault always exists) is not polynomial unless P = PSPACE; Cao et al. gave an algorithm in time exponential in the square of states, since improved by Miao et al.
numbers: No exact bound readable in the extract.
limits: Reported via b11 only.
agent_relevance: Weak diagnosability fits an agent that can choose probes (it is allowed to act), strong diagnosability fits passive logs.

source: Plank & Wotawa (2026) related-work claims on other LLM diagnosis studies
finding: The paper states that Qaid et al. tested four open-source models on machine fault diagnosis and found them as good as established deep-learning methods, and that Lukens et al. combined models with manuals and stressed careful evaluation. The authors found no earlier systematic study of small local models on text diagnosis with multi-category manual scoring.
numbers: 4 open models (Qaid et al.); no accuracy given in this text.
limits: Second-hand summaries; I did not open those papers.
agent_relevance: The LLM literature has no study of diagnosability itself (can any test separate candidates); this is a gap our scaffold can fill with simple code checks.

source: Plank & Wotawa (2026) ChatGPT demo, Fig. 1
finding: Free ChatGPT, given a two-bulb parallel circuit (L1 lit, L2 dark), gave only correct diagnoses and listed distinguishing tests (swap bulbs, measure voltage, continuity). The authors flag the circuit is a standard literature example and may be memorised.
numbers: Single anecdotal conversation, April 2026.
limits: N = 1, not a controlled test; authors speculate about hidden diagnostic procedures.
agent_relevance: Models can name separating tests for textbook cases; the open question is whether they do so for novel systems.

source: Marozzo & Lio (2026) pool-versus-choice gap
finding: The gap between potential and final score measures what the model could not separate from the evidence. The authors say the gap alone cannot distinguish missing evidence from selection error. This is the practical symptom of non-diagnosability.
numbers: Gap = potential minus final: SIA 10.0; ToT 22.5; THK-int 11.9; ReAct 17.5; BAS 13.9 (computed from Table 1).
quote: The potential-final gap alone cannot distinguish missing evidence from selection errors.
limits: Gaps computed by me from table values; potential uses oracle access to the reference answer.
agent_relevance: Log the gap in our benchmarks and add a check: can any question in the set separate the top two candidates?

source: Ibrahim et al. (2017) running assumptions
finding: Diagnosability is a design-time property tied to a belief state: it can hold at nominal start and fail after a repair or fault because the belief is more uncertain.
numbers: Not numeric.
quote: suffering thus in general from uncertainty and from being different from the initial nominal state for which diagnosability was ensured by design
limits: Domain: power networks, discrete event models.
agent_relevance: Re-test separability after each state change; a test set that worked at S0 may not work once evidence has moved the belief.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) experimental design and contamination control
finding: Examples were made by hand and solutions released after the models' release, to avoid training leakage. Step-wise grading fed correct inputs to each step so errors did not carry forward. Reasoning effort was high for the dedicated approach and medium for the broad one.
numbers: temperature 0, top_p 0 for 4o-mini; footnote: gpt-4o and 4o-mini had near-zero accuracy on unseen examples without code.
limits: Only OpenAI models; small examples.
agent_relevance: Copy this method for our test sets: unseen, hand-made, graded per step.
